verification_report.summary:
The candidate is correct relative to the explicitly accepted internal inputs. Fifteen sequential statement checks and five internal-reference checks found no critical errors or gaps. The audit includes the density lemma, entropy corollary, normalized-equation application and varying-reference consequence; it is not a novelty assessment or a certification of the entire manuscript.

Ordinary type means bounded additive equivalence. It transfers the genuine smaller-background envelope from phi to u. Zero density is excluded by strict domination applied to u and u+1. For N=||F||_q>0, the bounded-subsolution lemma applies to F/N in the fixed big semipositive background (1-epsilon)theta with Lq norm one. For h=P_{epsilon theta}(phi)+s, one has h<=phi<=u+C, hence h+t preceq u. Positive bounded mixed products on finite truncation levels, followed by locality and exhaustion, give MA_theta^ext(h)>=(b_q/N)F dV. The pole set has zero smooth volume. If N<b_q, strict domination with a=u, b=h+t and r=N/b_q forces u>=h+t for every t, contradicted at a common finite point. The resulting b_q is independent of phi for fixed geometry, volume, theta, epsilon and q. This is a density-norm bound, not a uniform lower total-mass bound.

Applying the lemma to c exp(G) gives B_phi(G)>=log b_q-(1/q)log integral exp(qG)dV. For the upper comparison, choose one Hermitian Omega>=theta and a bounded Omega solution v with scalar c_Omega. Constants provide a genuine smaller-background envelope for v, while u+t preceq v. Positive smooth enlargement gives MA_Omega^ext(u)>=c exp(G)dV. If c>c_Omega, strict domination with a=v, b=u+t and r=c_Omega/c forces v>=u+t for every t, again impossible at a finite point. Therefore B_phi<=B_{Omega,0} and H_phi<=H_{Omega,0}. Infinite auxiliary extended masses are permitted: no signed unrestricted product or subtraction of infinite measures occurs.

The continuous-test entropy variational formula, with the bijection K=qG, gives the lower entropy coefficient exactly 1/q and a_q=log b_q. The independently established Hermitian upper bound gives A+n Ent. Absolutely continuous probabilities with infinite entropy have infinite H_phi by the lower bound; every probability that is not absolutely continuous has both values infinite. H_phi never equals minus infinity. Finite domains and uniformly bounded families coincide by fixing q=2. The constants are uniform in the reference for common theta and epsilon. The proof also covers dimension one and assumes neither BMP nor PVP; individual noncollapse from bigness is not a uniform lower-mass hypothesis.

The proposed normalized-equation simplification is valid and noncircular. Since sup v_j=0, the density lemma yields b_p<=||c_j exp(v_j/j)f||_p<=c_j||f||_p, hence c_j>=b_p/||f||_p>0. Together with the existing scalar upper bound, this permits extraction of c_j converging to c>0 directly and removal of the later separate zero-mass contradiction. The new lemma uses only the earlier bounded subsolution, positivity and singular strict domination, not either prescribed-type existence proof. The other convergence arguments remain necessary.

For arbitrary supporting probabilities with ||G_j||_infinity<=M, existing support duality and scalar comparison give H_{phi_j}(nu_j)<=L_0=B_{Omega,0}(0)+2M. Thus Ent(nu_j)<=E_0=2(L_0-log b_2), and H_{Omega,0}(nu_j)<=A+nE_0. This places them in one fixed finite Hermitian dual sublevel, proving uniform integrability and relative weak-L1 compactness. Weak limits remain in that sublevel and have finite entropy; entropy lower semicontinuity also preserves the bound E_0. The chapter's measurable-support extension covers bounded measurable logarithmic densities as well. No identification with a limiting reference's supporting set, strong L1 convergence, singular-reference mass equality, entropy-difference extrema or new mass-attainment formula is claimed.
